subject: chemistry
title: Laboratory apparatus and key terms
key_idea: Choose apparatus for the quantity and the accuracy needed: stop-watch for time, thermometer for temperature, balance for mass, and cylinders, burettes, pipettes and gas syringes for volume. Know the terms solvent, solute, solution, saturated solution, residue and filtrate.

blocks.text: Each apparatus measures one quantity. Choose the one that gives the accuracy the experiment needs.

rows: Time a reaction or take readings at set intervals.
Measure the temperature of a liquid or mixture.
Weigh a solid or a container.
Measure any volume, as accurately as possible, by running it out.
Measure one fixed volume very accurately.
Collect and measure a gas given off.

diagram.alt: An explorer of laboratory apparatus. Tap each piece to see what it measures.
diagram.prompt: Tap each piece of apparatus to learn what it measures, then test yourself.

parts.name: Stop-watch
parts.detail: Measures time, for example how long a reaction takes or when to take a reading.

parts.name: Thermometer
parts.detail: Measures temperature, for example the start and end temperature of a mixture.

parts.name: Balance
parts.detail: Measures the mass of a solid, a liquid or a container.

parts.name: Measuring cylinder
parts.detail: Measures volumes of liquid quickly. It is less accurate than a burette or pipette.

parts.name: Burette
parts.detail: Measures any volume of liquid accurately by running it out. Used in titrations.

parts.name: Volumetric pipette
parts.detail: Measures one fixed volume of liquid, such as 25.0 cm³, very accurately.

parts.name: Gas syringe
parts.detail: Collects and measures the volume of a gas, for example from a reaction.

items: Match the apparatus to the quantity: time, temperature, mass or volume.
A burette and a pipette are more accurate than a measuring cylinder.
A pipette measures one fixed volume only.

blocks.text: You may be asked for the advantages and disadvantages of a method, or how to improve it.

rows: Burette or pipette instead of measuring cylinder
Can measure any volume, not just one
Less suited to one exact fixed volume
Polystyrene cup instead of glass beaker
Insulates, so less heat is lost or gained
Cannot be heated with a flame
More points, so a better graph

items: Repeat and compare results to check they are **reliable**.
Use a water bath to keep a reaction at a steady temperature.
The first bubbles of gas collected are air from the apparatus, so they are not collected.
An improvement should say what to change and why it helps.
Insulation reduces heat loss. Repeats confirm reliability.

blocks.text: These words describe dissolving and separating. They are used in many experiments.

items.meaning: A substance that dissolves a solute.
A substance that is dissolved in a solvent.
A mixture of one or more solutes dissolved in a solvent.
A solution containing the maximum concentration of a solute dissolved in the solvent at a specified temperature.
A substance that remains after evaporation, distillation, filtration or a similar process.
A liquid or solution that has passed through a filter.

items: Rock salt is a mixture of salt and sand. In water the salt is the solute and the water is the solvent.
Filtering the mixture leaves the sand as the residue.
The salt solution that passes through the filter paper is the filtrate.
Evaporating the filtrate leaves salt crystals as the residue.
To make a solid dissolve faster, heat the mixture, stir it or crush the solid.
A solution is a solute dissolved in a solvent.
Saturated means the maximum amount is dissolved at that temperature.
The residue stays behind. The filtrate passes through.

checks.q: State which apparatus measures one fixed volume only.
Explain why a polystyrene cup gives more accurate temperature results than a glass beaker.
checks.a: Polystyrene is a better insulator, so less heat is lost to the surroundings.

checks.q: A mixture of salt and sand is filtered. Name the residue and the filtrate.
checks.a: The sand is the residue. The salt solution is the filtrate.

worked_example.question: Zinc sulfate crystals are produced by heating aqueous zinc sulfate until a saturated solution is formed. When the saturated solution cools down, crystals of zinc sulfate start to form. State what is meant by the term saturated solution.
answer_points: A solution containing the maximum amount of solute dissolved, so no more solute can dissolve.
worked_example.tip: The temperature is a separate mark, so include it.

worked_example.question: The box lists words that may be used to explain the term saturated solution: solute, solvent, temperature. Explain, using all the words in the box, the term saturated solution.
answer_points: A saturated solution contains as much solute as possible in a certain volume of the solvent.
At a particular (given or constant) temperature.
worked_example.tip: Use all three words from the box.
